items.title: 11.4 The equivalence between mass and energy

source_refs.note: Topic 11.4 (PDF 256, printed 253). The catalogue keeps the printed heading 'Equilance'.

blocks.text: According to the special theory of relativity, mass and energy are distinct entities but are interconvertible. The total energy E and mass m of an object are related by E = mc^2 ... (11.4), where m depends on the speed of the object.

At rest, the energy equivalent of an object's mass m0 is called its rest mass energy E0: E0 = m0 c^2. As mc^2 is greater than m0 c^2, the difference of energy (mc^2 - m0 c^2) is due to the motion and represents the kinetic energy of the mass: K.E. = (m - m0) c^2.

From Eq. 11.4, the change in mass delta m due to a change in energy delta E is delta m = delta E/c^2. Because c^2 is a very large quantity, small changes in mass require very large changes in energy. In our everyday world energy changes are too small to produce measurable mass changes; however, the energy and mass changes in nuclear reactions are found to agree exactly with these equations.

blocks.title: Mass-energy relations
blocks.text: E = mc^2 (11.4); rest mass energy E0 = m0 c^2; kinetic energy K.E. = (m - m0) c^2; delta m = delta E/c^2.
